description:
Notem connects ChatGPT to the notes you stored in your Notem account.

You can use it to:

• Search your notes by keywords or meaning and filter results by date or tag
• Read the full contents of a saved note
• Retrieve text from saved voice-note transcriptions
• Create new notes
• Add content to or update existing notes
• Add or remove tags
• Delete notes

Your Notem account can contain saved text, links, screenshots, voice-note transcriptions, project notes, code snippets, research, feedback, and other information you previously captured.

Example requests:

• “Find my notes about next video's inspiration.”
• “What notes did I save last Tuesday?”
• “Find the beta-user feedback I saved.”
• “Save this plan as a new note tagged roadmap.”
• “Add this decision to my existing pricing note.”

A Notem account is required. When you connect Notem, ChatGPT can access the notes available to your authenticated Notem account.

positive.description: Find notes about a topic using the default progressive search strategy.
positive.prompt: What did I save about pricing?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns matching saved notes with enough context to identify the relevant one.

positive.description: Review the user's most recently updated notes.
positive.prompt: What are my most recent notes?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the user's recently updated notes in recency order.

positive.description: Save a new decision as a note with a tag, then move it to the trash so the account is left as it was.
positive.prompt: Save this: We will use a $9 monthly floor. Tag it pricing. Then move that note to the trash.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a private note containing the decision with the pricing tag, then moves that same note to the trash and confirms both steps.

positive.description: Review which tags the collection uses and how much sits under each.
positive.prompt: What tags do I use in my notes, and which one has the most in it?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the user's tags with a live count of notes carrying each, and identifies the busiest.

positive.description: Correct a unique piece of text in an existing note, then change it back so the note is left as it was.
positive.prompt: In my team meeting note, change 'meet at 3' to 'meet at 4', then change it back to 'meet at 3'.
positive.expected_behavior: Replaces 'meet at 3' with 'meet at 4' in the team meeting note, then replaces it back, and confirms the note again reads 'meet at 3'.

negative.description: Do not trigger for calendar requests.
negative.prompt: What meetings do I have tomorrow?

negative.description: Do not trigger to browse or summarize an unsaved web page.
negative.prompt: Summarize this article for me: https://example.com/long-read

negative.description: Do not trigger to send communications.
negative.prompt: Email my landlord about the broken heating.
